concept.title: Using Impala with Iceberg REST Catalog

conbody.p: Iceberg REST Catalog Impala supports Apache Iceberg REST Catalog, which enables Impala to connect directly to Iceberg REST Catalog servers. This feature allows you to:

ul.li: Run Impala without Hive Metastore (HMS) or catalogd dependency
Connect to multiple REST catalog endpoints simultaneously
Use hybrid deployments with both HMS and REST catalogs
Integrate with open-source REST catalog implementations

conbody.p: For more information on the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog specification, see Iceberg REST Catalog.

The Iceberg REST Catalog is a standardized HTTP API for managing Iceberg table metadata. Unlike traditional Hive Metastore (HMS) deployments, REST Catalog provides a lightweight, cloud-native approach to catalog management that works seamlessly across different compute engines.

REST Catalog configuration in Impala uses Java properties files that specify connection details and authentication settings. Configuration files must be placed in a directory specified by the --catalog_config_dir flag.

section.title: Configuration File Format
section.p: Configuration files use the standard Java Properties format, with key=value pairs. Each file represents a separate REST Catalog.

section.title: Required Properties
section.p: The following properties are required in every REST Catalog configuration file:

ul.li: connector.name: Must be set to iceberg
iceberg.catalog.type: Must be set to rest
uri or iceberg.rest-catalog.uri: REST Catalog endpoint URL

section.title: Environment Variable Substitution
section.p: Impala supports environment variable substitution in .properties files to securely manage credentials and environment-specific settings. This feature is particularly useful for storing secrets outside of configuration files.

ul.li: Variable names must match the pattern: [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*
Environment variables must be set before starting Impala
Undefined variables will cause Impala startup to fail

conbody.p: Impala supports three deployment modes for REST Catalog, each suited to different use cases and architectural requirements.

section.title: Mode 1: Standalone REST Catalog (No HMS/Catalogd)
section.p: This mode runs Impala without HMS or catalogd, connecting directly to one or more REST Catalog servers. It provides the simplest architecture for pure Iceberg deployments.
Example Use Case: New deployments that only need Iceberg tables and want minimal operational complexity.

section.title: Mode 2: Multi-Catalog (REST Catalog(s) + HMS)
section.p: This hybrid mode connects to both REST Catalogs and HMS simultaneously, allowing access to both Iceberg tables in the REST Catalog and traditional HMS tables.
Example Use Case: Migration scenarios or environments that need both new Iceberg tables and legacy HMS tables.
If a table with the same name exists in multiple catalogs, queries will fail with an ambiguity error. The error message will indicate which catalogs contain the table.

conbody.p: A REST Catalog server can vend short-lived, table-scoped storage credentials to clients as part of the load table response, so that Impala does not need long-lived object store credentials configured on every host. Impala supports credential vending for tables stored on Amazon S3 and S3-compatible object stores accessed through the s3a:// filesystem.

section.p: Set the following property in the catalog configuration file. Impala then requests vended credentials from the REST Catalog server on every table load:

The REST Catalog server must also be configured to vend credentials for the warehouse; refer to the documentation of your catalog server. When the server does not return credentials for a table, Impala falls back to the credential resolution described below, so enabling the property on a catalog that vends nothing is harmless.
When using an S3-compatible object store (for example, MinIO), the endpoint is a cluster-wide setting and is not part of the vended credential. Configure it in core-site.xml:

section.title: Credential Precedence
section.p: When Impala opens a connection to a filesystem, it resolves the credential for the path in the following order. The first source that provides a credential wins:

ol.li: Vended credential: a credential vended for the table being queried whose storage prefix matches the path. If several prefixes match, the longest one is used.
Process-wide S3 credential: the access and secret key retrieved at startup through the --s3a_access_key_cmd and --s3a_secret_key_cmd impalad flags, if both are set.
Hadoop configuration: whatever credential provider chain is configured in core-site.xml, for example static keys, instance profiles, or a JCEKS credential store.

section.p: Vended credentials are looked up by the storage prefix they were vended for. Impala opens one filesystem connection per prefix and credential; concurrent queries on the same table share that connection, and a refreshed credential results in a new connection for the files opened after the refresh. During planning, the coordinator reads table metadata through a FileIO that opens each file with the credential vended for it, so no cluster-wide credential is needed for metadata reads either.

section.title: Token Lifetime and Refresh
section.p: Vended credentials are temporary and carry an expiry time. A long-running query can outlive the credential it started with, so Impala refreshes vended credentials during query execution:

ul.li: Before a file is opened, Impala checks the expiry of the credential matching its path. If it is within --credential_refresh_threshold_s seconds of expiring (default 300), the credential is refreshed first and the file is opened with the refreshed one.

The refresh is performed through the query coordinator, which asks the REST Catalog server for the table's current credentials and returns them to the executor. A single refresh is issued per table even when many threads request it at the same time, and a table is refreshed at most once per --credential_refresh_min_interval_s seconds (default 60).
A refreshed credential is used by every file opened afterwards. Reads that are already in progress continue on the connection they were opened with.

If a refresh fails, Impala logs a warning and keeps using the existing credential until it expires. Once expired, the credential is no longer used and file opens fall back to the next source in the precedence list above; a later successful refresh restores it.

section.p: Configure the credential lifetime on the REST Catalog server so that it comfortably exceeds the refresh threshold; otherwise every table is refreshed at the minimum interval for the whole duration of a query.

ul.li: Credential vending requires local catalog mode (--use_local_catalog=true); see .
Only S3 and S3-compatible storage accessed through s3a:// is supported. Credentials vended for other storage types are ignored.

For connections that use a vended credential, Impala replaces the fs.s3a.aws.credentials.provider chain with its own provider followed by the Hadoop default chain. A custom provider chain configured in core-site.xml still applies to all other connections.
Vended credentials apply to scans and to the metadata reads performed during planning. Spilling to S3 keeps using the process-wide or Hadoop configuration credential.

section.p: The following Iceberg REST Catalog features are not currently supported:

ul.li: User Sessions: Only NONE session type is supported. Per-user session isolation is not available.
Nested Namespaces: The nested-namespace-enabled property must be set to false. Only flat namespace hierarchies are supported.
Write Operations: Write operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE) are not supported.
DDL Operations: DDL operations (CREATE, ALTER, DROP,...) are not supported.
Views: Iceberg views are not supported through the REST Catalog.
